moves.heading: ### D74 — Bring-your-own model providers and subscription sign-in (M95, M95b, M95c, 2026-10-04)
moves.firstLine: The owner, 2026-10-04: "as an expansion to the byo agents i would like to
moves.summary: Bring-your-own model providers use one canonical format, with adapters only at the wire: `ModelApiHost` keeps building one body and reading one stream, and every provider other than Meta is the shared transport plus a codec behind the `ProviderClient` interface. A BYO model is referenced as `<providerId>/<modelId>`; Meta's models stay bare, so every Meta request, stored session and hook payload keeps its bytes. Providers live in one user-level file, `providers.json`, which never holds a credential, and every credential is bound to the exact origin it was obtained for. Transport is HTTPS only, with plain HTTP only to a loopback address. Prices drive budgets and are never guessed. Subscription sign-in (M95b) uses official, provider-sanctioned flows only; another application's client or stored tokens are never read or reused.
moves.reason: Shipped BYO-provider/subscription design record (M95/M95b); the rule paragraph stays. The union holds D74 twice (full record here, archived stub at the second occurrence); this move archives the record under the existing D74 archive heading and the join deletes the duplicate stub (see duplicates). No test or script cites these lines.

moves.heading: ### D49 — Coding quality first: what to build next (2026-09-27)
moves.summary: Coding quality first: the ranking rule (what most improves the code the user gets comes first — the model seeing its edits' effects, understanding the code, reading the pages it needs; then reviewing and shipping, fewer tokens on long tasks, more agents safely, connectivity; both-backends-first within a wave), the carried rules (model calls beyond the user's own turn are billed, opt in, priced and ask first; Restricted Mode runs no git or shell; token/quality trades ship only after M75's paired evaluation holds the floors; one-token ide-server tool constraints), and the M67–M85 wave batch it ordered (all shipped).
moves.reason: Shipped 2026-09 batch-ordering record (M67–M85 all shipped); the ranking rule and carried rules stay as the rule. No test or script cites these lines.

moves.heading: ### D118 — Refusals read by shape, retried by code, stored without leaks (lanes PROVERR round 2 + PROVERRR2, 2026-10-13; numbered D109 until 2026-10-17, renumbered with D117)
moves.firstLine: **Rule in force.** One extractor reads an error body by what it IS (an
moves.summary: One extractor reads an error body by what it IS, whatever the wire format; the status and the provider's documented type, code or reason decide the kind, a phrase only where a recorded answer shows the provider gives nothing else. Retry follows the preset's own table with the envelope code (a quota 429 never retries while a bare one does); Anthropic max_tokens maps as documented. Parity: a bad key reads authentication at all eleven recorded providers, an unknown model reads notFound at all twelve.
moves.reason: Shipped refusal-shape design record (PROVERR lanes, merged); the Rule-in-force paragraph stays as the rule. A src comment cites D118 as authority; the heading and rule stay, so it keeps resolving. No test or script cites these lines.
